findings.claim: The q:1 rationale and generator_meta.hedge_map.1 both characterise key C as an unhedged assertion, which the option's own wording contradicts and which the fresh G-STEM leg reads the opposite way. The teaching payload therefore asserts a hedge-status that is false on its face, and the sentence immediately preceding it in the same rationale describes exactly the hedge it goes on to deny.
findings.evidence: Shipped q:1 rationale, two consecutive sentences: ”Nyckeln uttalar sig därför om vad som är påvisbart i förväg, inte om hur stor besparingen till slut blir – det senare avstår hon uttryckligen från att prissätta. Nyckeln är här ett rakt, ohedgat påstående, inte det försiktigaste alternativet.” The first sentence names the epistemic scoping (påvisbart i förväg); the second denies any hedge. generator_meta.hedge_map.1 repeats it: ”key is a flat, unhedged assertion”. Counter-read from the fresh leg, verdicts-r3/verdicts-gstem.jsonl, target q:1, finding 1: ”C is the hedged twin of D (same direction, weaker force) with a double hedge, quantitative (’bara en bråkdel’) and epistemic (’påvisbar’), the classic key position.” Option C as shipped: ”Att bara en bråkdel av besparingen är påvisbar.” — ’bara en bråkdel’ quantifies down and ’påvisbar’ scopes to what can be shown, against D's flat absolute ’inte en enda krona’.
findings.why_not_blocking: Rule-10 compliance does not depend on this sentence. Rule 10 requires that the qualified-option heuristic not SELECT the key in more than half a unit's questions, and the round-5-corrected hedge_map.balance states the compliant position accurately: the heuristic points at B in q:1 (wrong, so it is punished) and in q:2 only removes C without singling out the key, i.e. it selects the key in 0 of 2. C is also genuinely unhedged in MODALITY (indicative ’är’, no modal softener), so the sentence is defensible in the narrow sense it may have meant. The defect is that it is stated flatly enough to mis-train a student's hedge heuristic, in a rationale whose own previous sentence says the opposite.
findings.disposition: Recorded, not repaired here. Smallest fix when the unit is next opened: replace ”ett rakt, ohedgat påstående” with a formulation that separates modality from magnitude, e.g. ”ett rakt påstående i modalitet, men avsiktligt avgränsat i omfång”, and mirror it in hedge_map.1. Rationale-local and metadata-local, so it pulls no gate.

findings.claim: The passage's closing line lends surface support to q:2 distractor C. Round 4 recorded this in repair_log[round 4].not_done and left it for the passage owner; round 5 did not revisit it, so it ships as-is for a second consecutive round.
findings.evidence: Passage, stycke 6: ”Vårterminens turer är redan lagda, och de ser likadana ut vare sig avståndsgränsen dras vid två eller tre kilometer.” Read without restricting the anaphor, this asserts that no tur differs with the gräns — which is what q:2 distractor C asserts: ”Ingen av de tjugotre morgonturerna skulle gå att korta om gränsen höjdes.” Stycke 3 denies it by naming två stickvägar whose avstickare ”skulle gå att stryka ur turplaneringen” for knappt 90 000 kronor.
findings.why_not_blocking: Three independent reasons, all re-checked on the shipping bytes. (1) ’de’ is anaphoric to ’Vårterminens turer’ — routes ALREADY LAID, hence identical either way — which is a temporal/administrative claim, not the counterfactual C makes. (2) The q:2 stem scopes the question to the adressgenomgång in stycke 3, where C is flatly refuted. (3) Empirically no solver fell for it: all four fresh G-KEY records (verdicts-r3/verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl) name C and refute it by the stickvägar, and the G-STEM blind pick is A, not C. C is also strictly stronger than the closing line (’skulle gå att korta’ vs ’ser likadana ut’), so a student choosing C on stycke 6 is answering a question that was not asked.
findings.disposition: Recorded, not repaired. Editing the passage pulls G-SPRÅK and G-REGISTER, which are currently recorded against a byte-identical passage; that re-gate cost is not justified by a distractor that four independent solvers refuted without hesitation. Recommended scoping if the passage is ever reopened for another reason: ”och de turerna ser likadana ut …”.

findings.stage_challenged: adjudication (V-FINAL ruling on the residual G-STEM major)
findings.claim: ADJUDICATED TOLERABLE — NO REPAIR. The stance-composition cross-question channel flagged as major-severity in verdicts-r3/verdicts-gstem.jsonl (both questions) is ruled inside the tolerable class and is not a blocker. Full reasoning in stance_channel_ruling below.
findings.evidence: G-STEM q:1 finding 2: ”Cross-question channel inside the sheet: q:2's four options are all about whether raising the limit would actually remove any tur, vehicle or stop, and no option anywhere in this sheet asserts that the saving is real — two q:1 options deny it, two dodge onto process. The sheet's own option composition therefore constrains the author's stance to savings-sceptical before any passage is read, which pushes the key into {C, D} and, with the absolutism tell on D, onto C.” G-STEM q:2 finding 2 runs the same channel the other direction: form alone gives a 1-in-3 floor over {A, B, D}, and ”admitting the same cross-question channel … narrows to {A, C}, and the hedged twin beats the absolute twin, landing on A.” Both are held at flag, not kill, and G-STEM's own qualifier is ”every link is a prior rather than a mechanism, hence major not lethal.”
findings.why_not_blocking: See stance_channel_ruling. Summarised: the channel is a genre prior that authentic UHR LÄS stance items exhibit at least as strongly (5 of 8 sampled, keys on the skewed side in all 5); it is already mitigated in both available directions inside this unit; and the only repair that would close it inserts a straw stance that converts a soft prior into a dead option, which is a net construct-validity loss.
findings.disposition: No repair. Lifted to bank policy — see recommendation in stance_channel_ruling.policy_recommendation so future G-STEM legs stop re-raising this as a per-item major.

findings.stage_challenged: structural leak (own hunt — a q:2 channel no leg named)
findings.claim: A residual blind channel on q:2 that G-STEM did not name: A and D read as a near-opposed pair, so an adversarial blind reader can narrow further than the 1-in-3 floor on record. The honest worst-case floor is 1-in-2, not 1-in-3.
findings.evidence: q:2 A: ”Nästan alla berörda elever åker med turer som ändå körs …” (most affected pupils use service that exists anyway). q:2 D: ”De flesta av hållplatserna i turlistorna trafikeras enbart för de berörda elevernas skull.” (most stops exist only for these pupils). These are not strict complements — round 5 correctly notes the denominators differ (elever vs hållplatser) — but they are the sheet's only quantified pair on the same underlying question, so a test-wise reader can strike C on absolutism and then treat {A, D} as the live opposition, discarding B as the odd one out.
findings.why_not_blocking: The narrowing terminates without a tiebreak. Both A and D carry the same class of hedge (’Nästan alla’ / ’De flesta’), so the qualified-option heuristic cannot separate them; pick-the-longest points at B (16 tokens / 103 chars) which the reader has just discarded, so it misfires twice over; and the conclusion-carrying tell splits 2-2. The floor is therefore 1-in-2 at the adversarial worst, still inside the PARTIALLY band the bank ships. Authentic precedent is direct: host-ver1-2019-verb1-LÄS-011 and its ver2 twin ship a full 2x2 mirror grid (A/C exact stance mirrors, B/D exact stance mirrors) in two exam versions, which narrows blind to a pair far more cleanly than this.
findings.disposition: Recorded so the number on record is the adversarial one rather than the leg's. No repair; closing it would require de-quantifying either A or D, and A's ’Nästan alla’ is the hedge that carries rule-10 balance on this question.

findings.claim: The two G-SPRÅK footnote items — the reviewer-facing anglicism ’hedgat’ and the snake_case English taxonomy labels embedded in Swedish rationale prose — are bank-wide convention in a field the spec defines as source material, not unit-local defects. Dispositioned info; no unit-local repair.
findings.evidence: In this unit: q:2 rationale ”Påståendet är hedgat (”nästan alla”) och avgränsat …”, and five snake_case labels inside Swedish sentences (”B är unsupported_causality och den intuitiva fällan”, ”C är overgeneralisation”, ”D är scope_shift”, ”A är detail_as_main”, ”B är plausible_worldknowledge”). Prevalence measured across the whole P5 bank (114 units with rationales in batches/*/candidates-final/): 112 of 114 carry snake_case taxonomy tokens in rationale prose; 30 of 114 carry hedgat/hedgad/hedgar. Spec, GENERATION.md line 266f: rationale ”This becomes Layer-2 explanation source material downstream — write it fully.” Downstream check: the shipped student-facing store /home/loucmane/dev/hpfetcher/data/explanations/ contains none of scope_shift, overgeneralisation, detail_as_main, plausible_worldknowledge or hedgat.
findings.why_not_blocking: The field is declared source material, not student copy; the labels are the trap taxonomy the pedagogy and integrated stages read against planted_traps; and the shipped student store demonstrates the downstream render already does not carry them. Repairing this unit alone would break the bank's internal consistency in 1 of 114 units and would strip the taxonomy the gates join on.
findings.disposition: No unit-local repair. Bank-level: the Layer-2 render step that converts these rationales into student copy must strip or translate the snake_case labels and replace ’hedgat’ with native Swedish (’reserverat’, ’med förbehåll’, ’avgränsat’). Worth writing into the render spec so it is not rediscovered per batch.

findings.claim: Two em dashes (U+2014) survive in the unit, against batch16 addendum rule 3 (’Spaced en dash ( – ) only; NEVER em dash (—)’). Both are in reviewer-facing metadata; every product surface is clean.
findings.evidence: Located by full-tree walk of the shipping JSON: generator_meta.repair_log[round 3].ticket (”… the flag sits on q:2 — that misattribution is corrected here by append …”) and generator_meta.repair_log[round 3].pedagogy_probe_round3 (”… re-argued after the rewrite — q:2 A is the only overlay finding …”). Product surfaces: passage contains 0 em dashes and 3 spaced en dashes; title, all 8 options and both rationales contain 0 em dashes.
findings.why_not_blocking: Rule 3 exists because the authentic corpus ratio is ~10 435:1 en dash to em dash in PASSAGE prose — it is a corpus-fidelity rule about what a student reads. Repair-log tickets are English reviewer prose that never reaches a student, and round 3's entry is now a historical record under the bank's never-rewrite practice, so editing it would be worse than leaving it.
findings.disposition: No repair. Noted only so the count on record is exact and no later leg reports it as a new finding.

findings.claim: generator_meta.originality_note is now roughly 5 000 characters of layered append-corrections, and the withdrawn false Öds- claim is still readable ahead of the paragraph that withdraws it.
findings.evidence: The field opens with the round-1 search log, which contains the sentence ”The municipality was renamed Ödsmyra: the element Öds- appears nowhere in the bank …”, and only later reaches ”CORRECTION 2026-08-26 (repair round 2 …). THE FALSE CLAIM, WITHDRAWN: the sentence above stating that ’the element Öds- appears nowhere in the bank’ is mechanically false …”, followed by the Flarkbro rename and the four-index verification log.
findings.why_not_blocking: This is exactly the bank's never-rewrite practice working as designed, and the withdrawal is explicit, quotes the false sentence verbatim, and gives re-runnable counter-evidence. The record as a whole is correct.
findings.disposition: No repair. Bank-level suggestion only: when a correction withdraws a claim in an append-only field, prepend a one-line ”SUPERSEDED IN PART — see CORRECTION at end” marker at the head of the field, so a reader who stops early is not left holding the withdrawn claim.

stance_channel_ruling.question: Is the stance-composition cross-question channel (G-STEM, verdicts-r3/verdicts-gstem.jsonl, major on both questions, held at flag) within the tolerable class, or does it require a repair before ship?
stance_channel_ruling.ruling: TOLERABLE. No repair. Recorded as finding F3 at severity note.
case_for_repair: The channel is CROSS-QUESTION, not intra-question. Authentic option-set skew lives inside one question; this alleges that q:1's option set is evidence about q:2's key and vice versa. The synthetic bank's standard is deliberately stricter than UHR's — it runs a dedicated G-STEM leg that UHR has no analogue for — so waving through a channel the bank's own gate named at major severity weakens the gate as an instrument.
This is a 2-question short. Half the sheet is evidence about the other half. In a 4-question LÄS long the same stance question would be diluted three ways; here the coupling is maximal.

The two questions each already have an independent better-than-chance form path (q:1: strike the absolute D, soft-strike the near-redundant caveat pair A/B, land on C; q:2: strike the absolute C, floor 1-in-3). The channel stacks on top of both rather than replacing either, so the unit's blind expected score sits meaningfully above 25 percent.

The repair is cheap in principle. A single q:1 option asserting that the budgeted saving is real would falsify the channel's premise outright, with no passage edit and no G-SPRÅK or G-REGISTER re-gate.
case_against_repair: EMPIRICAL: the authentic corpus skews at least this hard. I pulled every LÄS stance question from the 27-exam authentic bank (/home/loucmane/dev/hpfetcher/data/parsed/, prompts matching vad anser / vilken inställning / hur ställer sig / författarens hållning): 8 items. Five show exactly this composition skew, and in all five the key sits on the skewed side. host-2020-verb2-LÄS-015: all four options are criticisms of archival practice, 4-0 — you know blind the answer is a criticism. host-2022-verb2-LÄS-013 (kemiska bekämpningsmedel) is a near-exact structural twin of our q:1: no option asserts the pro position without qualification, two options are prescriptive ’bör’ stances and two are substantive claims, and the key is one of the substantive claims — the same 2-2 shape as our A/B (process stances) against C/D (substantive savings claims). host-2013-verb2-LÄS-020: 3 of 4 name a limit in the material, key among them. host-2023-verb2-LÄS-016: 3 of 4 critical, key critical. var-2025-verb2-LÄS-019: 3 limiting against 1 defending, key on the 3-cluster. Only host-ver1/ver2-2019-verb1-LÄS-011 is mirror-balanced, and var-2023-verb2-LÄS-018's skew is forced by its stem. A bank that forbade this would generate items LESS authentic than the target corpus.

MECHANISM vs PRIOR: G-STEM itself concedes ’every link is a prior rather than a mechanism’. Crucially the channel is a genre regularity, not a construction artefact: in any faithful debatt passage the author reports the findings that support her, so the key of a detail question will tend to align with her stance. That property is intrinsic to the genre and would survive any rewrite of these options.

DOUBLE-COUNTING ON q:1: the channel narrows q:1 only to {C, D}, because BOTH C and D are savings-sceptical. What actually decides between them is the absolutism tell on D — which is finding 1, an intra-question tell already counted. The channel contributes no independent decision power on q:1.

THE MITIGATIONS ARE ALREADY APPLIED, in both available directions. q:2 carries two pro-savings findings: B (vehicle count tracks eligible pupils) and D (most stops exist only for these pupils) — G-STEM's own q:2 finding 1 says so: ’both are substantive counter-positions to A (each implies the raise WOULD cut service, so the saving would be real)’. And q:1's A (’Att den behövs, men först vid nästa upphandling’) IS a pro-proposal stance, built on the concession the passage itself makes in stycke 4 (the empty-seats / 2029 procurement argument the author says she cannot dismiss). G-STEM's ’two dodge onto process’ undersells A: it asserts ’den behövs’. So the sheet's only genuine gap is on the narrow sub-axis ’is the budgeted 1,4 miljoner real’ — and the two G-STEM findings in the same file are in tension on exactly this point, since the q:2 finding concedes the sheet does carry pro-savings positions.

THE REPAIR IS A NET LOSS. The option that would close the channel — something like ’Att den ger den besparing som budgetunderlaget anger’ — is a straw stance in a signed critical column bylined by a nämnd member arguing against the proposal. No reader would entertain it. That converts a soft, defeasible prior into a hard dead option, dropping the effective option count from 4 to 3. Trading a prior for a dead option is a worse item, not a better one.

MEASURED FLOOR AND CLEAN SOLVES: G-STEM's own blind floor on q:2 is 1-in-3 on form alone (my own adversarial read gets it to 1-in-2, F4, still short of decided), and all four fresh G-KEY records reached the keys from the passage with unique, independently-argued derivations and zero kills.

RULE 10 IS DOING ITS JOB: the qualified-option heuristic selects the key in 0 of 2 questions here — it is actively punished in q:1, where the moderate-sounding B is wrong, and in q:2 it only removes C. The bank's designed anti-heuristic defence is engaged on precisely the question the channel targets.
stance_channel_ruling.decision_reasoning: The case for repair is strongest on its second and third points — a 2-question short couples maximally, and the channel stacks on two independent form paths. Those are real and I record the honest worst-case floor in F4 rather than the leg's more generous one. But the case for repair fails at its fourth point, which is where a ruling has to land: the only available repair makes the item worse. And it fails at its first point too, because the channel is not a defect the generator introduced. It is a property of single-author opinion prose that authentic UHR items exhibit at least as strongly, in the same section, the same question type, and — in host-2022-verb2-LÄS-013 — very nearly the same option architecture. A gate that named a genre regularity has done its job by naming it; the adjudication stage's job is to say whether it is actionable, and here it is not. The channel is therefore TOLERABLE: reportable, recorded, and not a blocker.
stance_channel_ruling.policy_recommendation: Lift this to bank policy rather than re-litigating it per item. Proposed wording for the next addendum: 'Stance-composition skew in single-author opinion passages (no option asserting the position the author is arguing against) is WITHIN TOLERANCE and is not a repairable structural leak, because authentic UHR LÄS stance items skew the same way or harder and the corrective option is a straw stance that dies on sight. Cross-question stance correlation is REPORTABLE at note severity but does not block, provided (a) no single question is blind-decidable on form alone, and (b) rule 10 holds. G-STEM should continue to name it; adjudication should not treat it as an open major.' Without this, the next batch will spend another round on the same finding.

cleared.result: q:1 = C, q:2 = A. Both unique, both passage-derivable, agreeing with the keys and with all four fresh G-KEY solves.
cleared.detail: q:1 = C. A is refuted verbatim by ”Någon ny avståndsgräns krävs inte för det” — the conceded 2029 procurement argument never becomes an endorsement of the raise. B has no textual anchor at all: her objection is to the belopp, not the takt, and she recommends starting somewhere else entirely (”vill nämnden hitta dem bör den börja i turplaneringen”). D is refuted by the conceded ”knappt 90 000 kronor”. C is carried by ”Den summan går inte att få fram ur kommunens egna turlistor” together with ”Det är den enda besparing som går att belägga i förväg”; 90 000 against 1 400 000 is 6,4 procent, a bråkdel. q:2 = A.
